package_info.why_malicious: OpenSSL 3.x versions contain two high-severity vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-3602 and CVE-2022-3786) that allow stack buffer overflows during TLS certificate verification, potentially leading to denial of service or, in rare configurations, remote code execution.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: CVE-2022-3602: 4-byte stack buffer overflow in ossl_punycode_decode() when processing X.509 certificates with malicious email addresses.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During TLS certificate verification, the code processes a maliciously crafted X.509 certificate, leading to a 4-byte stack buffer overflow, which may overwrite adjacent memory and potentially cause a crash or, in rare cases, remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Stack buffer overflows are classic vulnerabilities that can lead to memory corruption, crashes, or code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Certificate parsing should not allow user-controlled data to overwrite stack memory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; buffer overflows are never legitimate.
key_indicators: Stack buffer overflow in certificate parsing

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: CVE-2022-3786: Arbitrary-length stack buffer overflow in ossl_punycode_decode() when processing X.509 certificates with malicious email addresses, but attacker cannot control the overflown data.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During TLS certificate verification, the code processes a maliciously crafted X.509 certificate, leading to an arbitrary-length stack buffer overflow, which can cause a denial of service by crashing the process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Arbitrary-length stack buffer overflows can crash services and are a classic vector for denial of service or, in some cases, code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Certificate parsing should not allow user-controlled data to cause buffer overflows.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; buffer overflows are never legitimate.
key_indicators: Stack buffer overflow in certificate parsing

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious X.509 certificate with a specially crafted email address field.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious certificate is presented to a vulnerable OpenSSL 3.x client or server.

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable OpenSSL 3.x instance processes the malicious certificate during TLS handshake.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stack buffer overflow is triggered in ossl_punycode_decode().

attack_chain.action: Stack buffer overflow occurs, potentially causing a crash (DoS) or, in rare configurations, remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of service or, in rare cases, code execution.

behavioral_signatures: Crash of OpenSSL-based services during or immediately after certificate verification
Unusual or malformed X.509 certificates with long or specially crafted email address fields
Repeated TLS handshake failures with segmentation faults
file_indicators: Presence of ossl_punycode_decode in statically linked binaries (readelf -a [binary] | grep -i ossl_punycode_decode)
network_indicators: Inbound or outbound TLS connections involving certificates with suspiciously long or malformed email address fields
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for crashes or segmentation faults in OpenSSL-based services during TLS handshakes, especially when client certificate authentication is enabled. Scan binaries for the presence of vulnerable OpenSSL versions and the ossl_punycode_decode function. Analyze network traffic for X.509 certificates with unusually long or malformed email address fields. Use vulnerability scanners (e.g., JFrog Xray) to identify affected OpenSSL versions in your environment.
